newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY LEAGUE-BRITAIN DRAW TENSE OPENER ON NZ TOUR.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY LEAGUE-BRITAIN DRAW TENSE OPENER ON NZ TOUR.

text.p: Great Britain drew 22-22 with a Lion Red XIII on Thursday in a hard-fought opener to their New Zealand tour in Auckland.
Both sides missed chances to seal the match in the closing minutes, with Lion Red stand-off David Bailey hitting the post with a drop goal attempt and Britain having a try disallowed.

The tourists outscored the home side -- a composite line-up from the domestic competition -- four tries to three, but coach Phil Larder said after the game he was unhappy with his test-strength side's performance.
"I thought we played very badly," he said. "It should not have been a tough game but we made it tough by playing dumb football."
Lion Red scrum-half Ben Lythe kicked the first of five goals to open the scoring, but winger Anthony Sullivan replied quickly with a try.
The home side forged ahead with tries from hooker Tukere Barlow and forward Jonahan Hughes, but Britain pulled one back when fullback Stuart Spruce sprinted 85 metres for a solo try.
The visitors briefly pulled ahead in the second half with tries from hooker Keiron Cunningham and centre Daryl Powell, but Lythe tied up the match with a penalty goal.
